newsitem.title: ITALY: FAO sees global wheat stocks increasing in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: FAO sees global wheat stocks increasing in 96/97.

text.p: The U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) said on Monday that global wheat stocks were seen increasing by 11 percent to 117 million tonnes at the end of the 1996/97 crop seasons.
FAO said stocks of coarse grains were expected to increase by about 23 percent to 127 million tonnes.
Rice stocks were forecast to fall again for the fourth year in succession to 50 million tonnes by the end of 1997 from 53 million tonnes in 1995/96.
FAO's forecast for global cereal stocks at the end of 1996/97 remained unchanged at 294 million tonnes.

It said recovery in global cereal production in 1996 and expected replenishment of carryovers in the current 1996/97 season had eased the "exceptionally tight supply/demand situation of the previous year."

But it warned that the ratio of end-of-season stocks to trend use in 1997/98, now estimated at 16 percent, was still below the 17 to 18 percent range that FAO considers the minimum necessary to safeguard world food security.
